name: create_sh_rotate_logs
description: Writes a log-rotation script keeping the N newest files
prompts: Write rotate.sh: POSIX sh, invoked as `sh rotate.sh <dir> <keep>`. It looks at the *.log files directly inside <dir> and DELETES all but the <keep> newest ones (by modification time). Fewer than <keep> log files: delete nothing. It must only touch *.log files (never other files), handle filenames with spaces, print one line 'deleted: <filename>' (basename) per removed file, and exit 0. Exit 1 with a usage message if arguments are missing.

test_setup_files.test_rotate.py:
import os, subprocess, time

os.makedirs('logs', exist_ok=True)
names = ['old.log', 'mid dle.log', 'new.log', 'newest.log']
for i, n in enumerate(names):
    with open(f'logs/{n}', 'w') as f:
        f.write(n)
    t = time.time() - (400 - i * 100)
    os.utime(f'logs/{n}', (t, t))
with open('logs/keep.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('not a log')

r = subprocess.run(['sh', 'rotate.sh', 'logs', '2'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert r.returncode == 0, f'exit {r.returncode}: {r.stderr}'
left = sorted(os.listdir('logs'))
assert left == ['keep.txt', 'new.log', 'newest.log'], f'kept wrong files: {left}'
assert 'deleted: old.log' in r.stdout, r.stdout
assert 'deleted: mid dle.log' in r.stdout, f'spaced filename mishandled: {r.stdout!r}'

# fewer than keep: no deletions
r2 = subprocess.run(['sh', 'rotate.sh', 'logs', '5'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert r2.returncode == 0
assert sorted(os.listdir('logs')) == ['keep.txt', 'new.log', 'newest.log']

# missing args -> usage + exit 1
r3 = subprocess.run(['sh', 'rotate.sh'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert r3.returncode == 1, f'missing args must exit 1, got {r3.returncode}'
print('PASS')

reference_solution.rotate.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# rotate.sh <dir> <keep>: delete all but the <keep> newest *.log files.
if [ -z "$1" ] || [ -z "$2" ]; then
    echo "usage: rotate.sh <dir> <keep>" >&2
    exit 1
fi
dir=$1
keep=$2

# newest first; -t sorts by mtime. Filenames with spaces survive because we
# read line-by-line (log names contain no newlines).
ls -t "$dir"/*.log 2>/dev/null | awk -v k="$keep" 'NR > k' | while IFS= read -r f; do
    rm -f "$f"
    echo "deleted: $(basename "$f")"
done
exit 0

    echo "usage: rotate.sh <dir> <keep>" >&2
    exit 1
fi
dir=$1

ls -tr "$dir"/*.log 2>/dev/null | awk -v k="$keep" 'NR > k' | while IFS= read -r f; do
    rm -f "$f"
    echo "deleted: $(basename "$f")"
